title: Tax Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Bill 2013

divisions.question: Tax Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Bill 2013 - Consideration in Detail - Reject transparency provisions

speeches.speaker: Joe Hockey
speeches.brief: Criticised the chaotic handling of the Tax Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Bill, an 11-schedule bill denied any committee inquiry, and objected to a measure bringing forward $8 billion in company tax by shifting companies with turnover from $1 billion down to $20 million onto monthly tax instalments starting 1 January 2014.

speeches.speaker: Scott Buchholz
speeches.brief: Criticised the 11-schedule Tax Laws Amendment bill for being rushed through after the Labor-controlled Economics Committee refused an inquiry on 31 May 2013, said the PAYG instalment threshold was progressively lowered from $1 billion to $100 million to $20 million, and noted the measure was meant to help produce a forecast surplus but the government instead recorded a $19.4 billion deficit.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: Criticised the Tax Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Bill 2013 for being rushed through parliament without scrutiny, saying it contains more than $10 billion in additional revenue and represents what he called the single biggest revenue item in a tax laws amendment bill in the parliament's history.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Criticised the 118-page Tax Laws Amendment bill, introduced on 29 May, saying schedule 5 would require public disclosure of tax information for companies with $100 million or more in income, and detailed how the bill's staged PAYG instalment thresholds, falling from $1 billion on 1 January 2014 to $100 million on 1 January 2015 and $20 million on 1 January 2016, are intended to bring forward $10.15 billion in revenue over the forward estimates.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: Opposed schedules 3 and 4 of the bill regulating tax financial advice, quoting a 3 June letter from the Financial Planning Association warning the changes would affect its 9,000 members and likely more than 40,000 practitioners in total, and noted the House Economics Committee refused an inquiry into the bill on 31 May 2013.

speeches.speaker: Robert Oakeshott
speeches.brief: Defended the bill's tax transparency measure in schedule 5 for large corporations, supported schedules 3 and 4 bringing financial planners under a three-year transitional registration regime, and warned that with $1 trillion in superannuation savings at stake, weakening consumer protection regulation would be a mistake.

speeches.speaker: David Bradbury
speeches.brief: Responded that the PAYG instalment change in schedule 1 raises no additional tax and that the $20 million threshold was chosen to align with the GST monthly reporting threshold, and said schedule 2's new infrastructure tax loss incentive could benefit projects like Brisbane's Cross River Rail, Sydney's motorways and Melbourne Metro.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Moved that the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Corporations and Financial Services inquire into and report by 17 June 2013 on a proposed regulatory framework for tax financial advice services, focusing on its application, minimising regulatory duplication, its interplay with Future of Financial Advice reforms, and transitional relief for new advice providers.

speeches.speaker: Deb O'Neill
speeches.brief: Presented the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Corporations and Financial Services' report, with a dissenting report, on the regulatory framework for tax financial advice services covering schedules 3 and 4 of the Tax Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Bill 2013.

speeches.speaker: Deb O'Neill
speeches.brief: Argued for enacting the tax financial advice reforms to bring financial advisers into the Tax Agent Services regime, warning that letting the current exemption lapse on 30 June would leave advisers unable to comply, and noted a three-year transition period would run until the full regime commences on 1 July 2016.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: Opposed rushing schedules 3 and 4 of the Tax Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Bill into law, citing witness testimony of unresolved questions and no proper cost-benefit analysis, and recommended in the coalition's dissenting report extending financial planners' existing exemption from the Tax Agent Services Act by a further 12 months.

speeches.speaker: Christopher Back
speeches.brief: The report of the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Corporations and Financial Services on the regulatory framework for tax (financial) advice services was presented, and the Senate was moved to take note of it.

speeches.speaker: Anne McEwen
speeches.brief: The Economics Legislation Committee presented its report on the Tax Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Bill 2013, including the Hansard record and related documents, and ordered the report to be printed.

acts.title: Tax Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 2) Act 2013
